comments.content: Gating on `isOffline` alone also skips files that Immich actually owns. For external libraries the derived live-photo motion asset is stored in the encoded-video folder and is itself flagged `isOffline` by the library scan (its path is never inside an import path), and its `ASSET_DELETION` job inherits the parent's `deleteOnDisk`. With this guard the generated `*-MP.mp4` is never removed (while its thumbnail/preview are still queued for deletion), leaving orphan files in the media location. Consider only protecting originals that live outside Immich's media location, e.g. `asset.isOffline && !StorageCore.isImmichPath(asset.originalPath)`.

So the new handler guard means the -MP.mp4 file in encoded-video will not be deleted upon asset deletion even in the trash-empty flow. That is a leak introduced by the new guard (previously willDelete=true deleted it). Is that "wrong"? Yes, since encoded-video is Immich-owned storage; deleting the asset row without deleting the derived video leaves an orphan file. Also, the motion asset's `thumbnail/preview` still get deleted (they are pushed unconditionally), showing that Immich-managed generated files are intended to be deleted even for offline assets. comments.content:
This assertion is both flaky and currently incorrect:
1. The preceding test `should move an asset to the trash` (line 770) leaves an admin-owned asset with `status = TRASHED` and `deletedAt` set. `getAssetStatistics` is scoped to `auth.user.id` and counts `deletedAt IS NOT NULL AND status = TRASHED`, so `total` will be at least 1 here, not 0.
2. Force deletion is asynchronous: `deleteAll` only flips the status and queues an `ASSET_DELETION` background job, so the statistics must be read after the job completes (e.g. `waitForWebsocketEvent({ event: 'assetDelete', id: assetId })`).

Suggestion: capture the trashed total before the force delete and assert the delta after waiting for the deletion event.

const after = await getAssetStatistics({ isTrashed: true }, { headers: asBearerAuth(admin.accessToken) });
      expect(after.total).toBe(0);

comments.content:
This renamed test no longer exercises the behavior this PR introduces. The asset is made offline only via an exclusion pattern, which in `LibraryService.handleSyncAsset` sets `deletedAt` but leaves `status = ACTIVE`. `TrashRepository.empty()` only updates rows with `status = TRASHED`, so `/trash/empty` does not touch this asset at all (count is 0) and the test passes trivially. Additionally, the `existsSync` assertion that proves offline files are kept on disk was moved into the skipped test, so a regression in `asset.service.ts` (`willDelete` / `deleteOnDisk: !asset.isOffline`) would not be caught by any active test.

Suggestion: actually trash the asset first (`await utils.deleteAssets(admin.accessToken, [asset.id])`) so `/trash/empty` picks it up, then after `waitForQueueFinish(...,'backgroundTask')` assert both that the record is soft-deleted and that `${testAssetDir}/temp/offline/offline.png` still exists on disk.

Silently returning when the source is missing makes setup failures invisible. All call sites in `library.e2e-spec.ts` rely on the rename to drive the online/offline transition, and some tests would still pass for the wrong reason if the rename silently no-op'd (e.g. `should not set an offline asset to online if ... is covered by an exclusion pattern`: the final "still offline" assertions hold whether the file was restored and then excluded, or never restored at all). Consider letting `renameSync` throw (or explicitly assert existence) so a broken precondition surfaces as a setup error instead of a partially valid test.

This assertion cannot verify what the (skipped) test claims. Offline assets created by library sync keep `status = ACTIVE`, while `AssetRepository.getStatistics` only counts rows with `deletedAt IS NOT NULL AND status = TRASHED`; `after.total` is therefore 0 whether or not the offline asset was actually purged. When the test is re-enabled it would pass even if nothing was deleted. Assert the asset removal directly, e.g. `await expect(utils.getAssetInfo(admin.accessToken, asset.id)).rejects.toThrow()` or `searchAssets({ libraryId, withDeleted: true }).count === 0`. Note also that the `createImageFile` call above re-creates a file that was never removed (exclusion patterns only soft-delete the asset), so it does not change the state under test.
